html:
French Morocco was the French protectorate over most of Morocco from 1912 to 1956. The sultan of the Alaouite dynasty kept his throne, but French officials ruled.

The Treaty of Fez of 1912 set it up. The first resident general, Hubert Lyautey, left the old medinas alone and built new European towns beside them. Casablanca grew from a small port into the country's biggest city. Conquest of the Atlas mountains went on into the 1930s, and France joined Spain to defeat the Rif rising in the Rif War.

A 1930 decree that put Berber areas under customary law instead of Islamic law angered townspeople and gave birth to the nationalist movement. Sultan Mohammed V came to back independence. France exiled him in 1953, then brought him back in 1955, and Morocco became independent in 1956, together with Spanish Morocco. The later state is on the page Morocco.
sum: French Morocco was the French protectorate over most of Morocco from 1912 to 1956. The sultan of the Alaouite dynasty kept his throne, but French officials ruled.
